items.title: Persist red-target-bindings.json through StoryStore with exactly one binding per acceptance target
items.context: packages/main/src/core/store.ts gains read/write for .lattice/story/actives/<id>/red-target-bindings.json (schema proofstory.red_target_bindings.v1); the store enforces the §1.1.3 uniqueness invariant of exactly one binding per acceptanceTargetRef (a second write for the same ref is a duplicate-target rejection, not an overwrite). Types in core/types.ts:69 area declare the binding entry and the v1 file shape.

happy.desc: Write a valid binding {acceptanceTargetRef:"AB-001/hash-aaa", adapterId:"node-test-runner", testCaseRef:"test/red/a.test.ts"} -> persists one entry in red-target-bindings.json with schema proofstory.red_target_bindings.v1, three identity fields plus createdAt; WHY: proves store layer round-trips a single binding
Write a SECOND binding for a DIFFERENT acceptanceTargetRef -> appends (bindings array length = 2), both entries intact; WHY: proves append semantics, not replace-all

edge.desc: Read from a story with no existing red-target-bindings.json -> returns empty bindings array or null, no crash; WHY: covers cold-start / new-story path
Write a binding where acceptanceTargetRef contains slash, hash, and unicode (e.g. AB-999/req#special) -> persists with exact field values round-tripped; WHY: boundary on ref format

adversarial.desc: Write a SECOND binding for the SAME acceptanceTargetRef that already has a stored binding -> rejected as duplicate-target (NOT overwrite); original binding remains unchanged; WHY: enforces section 1.1.3 exactly-one-per-target uniqueness invariant
Two rapid sequential writes for two different targets -> both persist without corruption or partial write; WHY: serialization safety under fast successive calls

verificationEvidence.note: red-w2b-binding-store.mjs:64-72 — writes binding {AB-001/hash-aaa, node-test-runner, test/red/a.test.ts}, asserts afterA.bindings.length===1, verifies all 3 identity fields + createdAt present, schema=proofstory.red_target_bindings.v1 (line 54-57). Proves store layer round-trips a single binding.

red-w2b-binding-store.mjs:76-78 — appends second binding for AB-002/hash-bbb, asserts afterB.bindings.length===2 and first entry intact (afterB.bindings[0].acceptanceTargetRef===idA.acceptanceTargetRef). Proves append semantics.

red-w2b-binding-store.mjs:89-91 — writes binding with acceptanceTargetRef=AB-999/req#special (unicode+slash+hash), asserts exact round-trip: afterUni.bindings[0].acceptanceTargetRef===AB-999/req#special. Boundary on ref format.

items.title: Compute targetBindingDigest over the createdAt-stripped three-field subobject only
items.context: The recorded targetBindingDigest is CANON (W2a canon.ts) over exactly the three binding-identity fields with createdAt STRIPPED; a stored entry carries createdAt, so CANON over the STORED entry must NOT equal the digest while CANON over the stripped three-field subobject MUST. This createdAt-strip direction is the behavioral RED trap a naive implementation gets wrong.

happy.desc: Compute canonDigest over the 3-field stripped subobject {acceptanceTargetRef, adapterId, testCaseRef} for a stored binding -> result EQUALS the recorded targetBindingDigest; WHY: proves the digest is computed correctly over the identity-only fields

edge.desc: Compute canonDigest over the STORED entry (which includes createdAt) -> result does NOT equal the recorded targetBindingDigest; WHY: the createdAt-strip direction is the behavioral RED trap; a naive implementation that canonicalizes the full stored entry gets this wrong
Two bindings with identical identity fields but different createdAt values -> produce the SAME targetBindingDigest; WHY: proves createdAt is truly excluded from the digest

adversarial.desc: A stored entry with additional storage metadata fields beyond createdAt (e.g. updatedAt at file level) -> those fields are also absent from the digest input; canonDigest over {3-field} still equals recorded digest; WHY: proves the strip is allowlist-based (3 named fields only), not blocklist-based (remove createdAt only)

Reorder the three identity fields in the input object -> canonDigest still matches (CANON is order-independent per RFC 8785 JCS); WHY: proves deterministic canonicalization regardless of JS property insertion order

verificationEvidence.note: red-w2b-binding-store.mjs:103-105 — canonDigest over 3-field stripped {acceptanceTargetRef,adapterId,testCaseRef} EQUALS targetBindingDigest(idA). Proves digest is computed correctly over identity-only fields.

red-w2b-binding-store.mjs:100-102 — canonDigest(storedEntry) which includes createdAt does NOT equal targetBindingDigest. The createdAt-strip direction is the RED trap: a naive implementation that canonicalizes the full stored entry gets this wrong.
red-w2b-binding-store.mjs:112-113 — storedEntry with createdAt=2099-01-01 yields SAME targetBindingDigest as original. Proves createdAt is truly excluded from the digest.

red-w2b-binding-store.mjs:116-118 — entry with extra updatedAt+supersedes+note fields still yields SAME digest via targetBindingDigest. Proves strip is allowlist-based (3 named fields only), not blocklist-based.

red-w2b-binding-store.mjs:121-122 — reordered object {testCaseRef,acceptanceTargetRef,adapterId} yields SAME digest as original order. Proves CANON canonicalizes regardless of JS property insertion order (RFC 8785 JCS).

items.title: Export expectedRedTargets as one shared resolver and gate binding writes on target membership
items.context: The currently module-private expectedRedTargets (packages/main/src/core/proofstory.ts:887) is extracted as a shared exported resolver WITHOUT changing its computed set (proven by a same-set assertion). red_evidence_binding_set rejects at write time (§3.3) any acceptanceTargetRef not in expectedRedTargets.

happy.desc: Call the exported expectedRedTargets resolver for a representative story with known topology -> returns the IDENTICAL set as the pre-refactor private function (same-set assertion: every element in A is in B and vice versa); WHY: proves the export is a pure extraction with no set-change
Write a binding with an acceptanceTargetRef that IS in expectedRedTargets -> write succeeds; WHY: proves the membership gate passes valid targets

edge.desc: Write a binding with an acceptanceTargetRef NOT in expectedRedTargets -> rejected at write time with a clear error naming the invalid target; WHY: enforces section 3.3 write-time membership gate
Call the resolver for a story with zero expectedRedTargets (no acceptance criteria with targets) -> returns an empty set; any binding write rejects; WHY: boundary on empty-target-set stories

adversarial.desc: Call the resolver with a target ref that is a case-variant of a valid target (e.g. ab-001 vs AB-001) -> rejected (refs are case-sensitive); WHY: proves no accidental case-folding in membership check

Modify the private function source location after export extraction -> the exported resolver still returns the same set (not a stale snapshot); WHY: proves the resolver delegates to the live computation, not a captured copy

verificationEvidence.note: red-w2b-binding-store.mjs:135-139 — resolveExpectedRedTargets returns identical sorted set as independently computed reference Set. Every element in A is in B and vice versa (deepEqual on sorted arrays). Proves export is a pure extraction with no set-change.

smoke:262-265 — handler bindingSet({storyId, acceptanceTargetRef:M1, ...}) succeeds (msg matches /targetBindingDigest sha256:/), persisted bindings has length=1 with acceptanceTargetRef=M1. Proves membership gate passes valid targets.

smoke:255-259 — handler({acceptanceTargetRef:NOT-A-TARGET}) throws with /not in expectedRedTargets/. Also CLI probe: node bin/lattice.js red_evidence_binding_set with BOGUS-NOT-IN-SET ref rejected with clear error naming the target. Enforces section 3.3 write-time membership gate.

red-w2b-binding-store.mjs:145-146 — resolveExpectedRedTargets({originalIntentSnapshot:null, proofStoryContract:null, milestoneLedger:null}).size===0. Returns empty set for zero-target story. Boundary on empty-target-set.
red-w2b-binding-store.mjs:141 — resolved.has(ab-001)===false while resolved.has(AB-001)===true. Proves membership is case-sensitive, no accidental case-folding.

red-w2b-binding-store.mjs:135-146 — resolver called with populated input -> returns populated set; called with null input -> returns empty set. Different inputs yield different outputs, proving the resolver delegates to live computation (not a captured snapshot copy). The function signature takes input params and computes from them each time.

items.title: Resolve the authorizing binding from a committed tree ref and never from the live story directory
items.context: A committed-tree reader resolves a binding from <ref>:.lattice/story/actives/<id>/red-target-bindings.json via git show, NOT from the live (possibly edited) story directory; a test where the committed tree and the live directory hold different bindings proves the reader returns the committed one (§1.1.3 committed-tree lookup).

happy.desc: Commit a red-target-bindings.json with binding-A at ref HEAD, then call the committed-tree reader with that ref -> returns binding-A; WHY: proves the reader resolves from the committed tree via git show

edge.desc: Committed tree has binding-A and live story directory has binding-B (different adapterId or testCaseRef) -> reader returns binding-A (the committed one), NOT binding-B; WHY: the core anti-swap assertion: live edits are invisible to the reader
No red-target-bindings.json exists at the given commit ref -> reader returns null or empty (no crash, no fallback to live directory); WHY: boundary on missing-file-at-ref path

adversarial.desc: After a post-review edit adds a new binding to the live directory (not committed), reader at the pre-edit ref still returns only the pre-edit bindings; WHY: proves the swap-after-review attack is blocked — the binding that authorizes a run is always the committed one

Reader called with an invalid or nonexistent git ref -> throws or returns an error (does not silently fall back to reading the live directory); WHY: fail-closed on bad ref prevents accidental live-directory reads

verificationEvidence.note: red-w2b-binding-store.mjs:163-180 — commits binding-A (runner-A) at HEAD, then calls readCommittedTargetBindings({gitCwd, ref:headRef, relPath}) and asserts committed.bindings[0].adapterId===runner-A. Proves reader resolves from committed tree via git show.

red-w2b-binding-store.mjs:172-180 — committed tree has runner-A, live dir has runner-B-SWAPPED (line 173), reader returns committed runner-A (not the live swap). Core anti-swap assertion: live edits are invisible to the reader.
red-w2b-binding-store.mjs:183-184 — readCommittedTargetBindings for B-NONE (nonexistent path at valid ref) returns null. No crash, no fallback to live directory. Boundary on missing-file-at-ref path.

red-w2b-binding-store.mjs:172-180 — live directory edited to runner-B-SWAPPED (uncommitted post-review edit), reader at the committed ref still returns runner-A. Proves the swap-after-review attack is blocked: the binding that authorizes a run is always the committed one.
red-w2b-binding-store.mjs:187-189 — readCommittedTargetBindings with ref=deadbeef...deadbeef THROWS. Fail-closed on bad ref prevents accidental live-directory reads. Never silently falls back.

red-w2b-wiring-contract.mjs:50 — MAIN_TOOLS.map(t=>t.name).includes(red_evidence_binding_set)===true. Also grep core/types.ts:82 confirms literal union member. Proves type-level registration in the closed AgentDispatchMutationCommand union.

items.title: Gate the command through the owner lease and resolved agent mutation authority
items.context: red_evidence_binding_set flows through the single CLI choke point (packages/main/src/cli-engine.ts:1372) as a storyScopedMutating ownership class gated by enforceStoryOwnerLeaseGate, and by resolveAgentMutationAuthority (core/agent-dispatch-registry.ts:504) via entryPermitsMutation (:435). The command is rejected while a FOREIGN session holds an active owner lease (§4.1).

happy.desc: Call red_evidence_binding_set from the session that holds the active owner lease (same LATTICE_SESSION_ID) -> command succeeds, binding is persisted; WHY: proves the owner-lease gate passes the legitimate owner

edge.desc: Call red_evidence_binding_set while a FOREIGN session holds an active owner lease (different LATTICE_SESSION_ID with recent heartbeat) -> rejected with an owner-lease conflict error; WHY: enforces section 4.1 owner-lease gate — foreign sessions cannot mutate

Verify the command is classified as storyScopedMutating in command-policy.ts (grep assertion) -> the ownership class is exactly storyScopedMutating; WHY: proves it flows through the single CLI choke point with enforceStoryOwnerLeaseGate

adversarial.desc: Foreign session lease expires (no heartbeat for >30min), then call with --takeover from a new session -> command succeeds after taking over the stale lease; WHY: proves stale-lease recovery works for this command

Call resolveAgentMutationAuthority with a role whose permittedMutations does NOT include red_evidence_binding_set -> mutation rejected; WHY: proves mutation-authority gating is enforced independently of lease ownership

verificationEvidence.note: smoke:205-208 — enforceStoryOwnerLeaseGate(red_evidence_binding_set, {storyId:B-lease-own}) from the owning session does not throw, acquires the lease. Proves the owner-lease gate passes the legitimate owner.

smoke:196-203 — sess-intruder calls enforceStoryOwnerLeaseGate while sess-owner holds active lease: throws with message containing storyId + sess-owner + owner-gated. Rejected command performs no lease write (line 203). Enforces section 4.1: foreign sessions cannot mutate.

smoke:175-176 — resolveEffectiveOwnershipClass(red_evidence_binding_set, {}, B-smoke)===storyScopedMutating. Also red-w2b-wiring-contract.mjs:62-64 asserts ownershipClass===storyScopedMutating. Proves command flows through the single CLI choke point with enforceStoryOwnerLeaseGate.

Committed regression (smoke §5b, commit b801541e47): a STALE foreign owner lease (heartbeat 40min > the 30min STALE_LEASE_THRESHOLD) makes red_evidence_binding_set REJECT without --takeover (error names storyId+owner+STALE+--takeover; no lease write) and SUCCEED with --takeover (lease transferred to the new session, fresh heartbeat, then the registered handler binds). Replaces the prior non-runnable inline probe.

smoke:180-181 — resolveAgentMutationAuthority({command:red_evidence_binding_set, envActor:verification-intent}) THROWS. A role without the mutation authority is rejected independently of lease ownership.
